scientific.integrity: The source bias-corrected StableAdamW recurrence is solved exactly on a deterministic one-coordinate gradient impulse. The proof keeps the positive numerical floor \(\varepsilon\) and distinguishes a uniform family statement from the decay of any fixed finite impulse.
limitations: One scalar coordinate with zero weight decay and a deterministic externally prescribed impulse.
Input-response result rather than a fixed-objective convergence or divergence theorem.
Unboundedness is over finite impulse amplitudes and observation times; every fixed finite impulse eventually decays when \(\varepsilon>0\).
The source's reported \((\beta_1,\beta_2)\) settings lie on the bounded side.
Tensor averaging in the clipping statistic and cross-coordinate effects are outside scope.

title: StableAdamW's current-gradient clip has a sharp impulse-tail boundary
